title: 1978 AHSME Problem 13
statement: If \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c,\) and \(d\) are nonzero numbers such that \(c\) and \(d\) are the solutions of \(x^2+ax+b=0\) and \(a\) and \(b\) are the solutions of \(x^2+cx+d=0,\) then \(a+b+c+d\) equals

solutions.text:
Vieta’s formulas give \[ \begin{aligned} c+d&=-a,& cd&=b,\\ a+b&=-c,& ab&=d. \end{aligned} \] The two sum equations imply \(b=d.\) Since \(b=d\ne0,\) the product equations give \(a=c=1.\) Then \(a+b=-c\) gives \(b=d=-2,\) and therefore \(a+b+c+d=-2.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
